# Use a common base image like Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set environment variables to enable non-interactive installation
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build-time dependencies, runtime dependencies, MPI, and certificates
# This includes build-essential, cmake, git for building,
# and openmpi, fftw, libgomp1 for running LAMMPS with ReaxFF.
# CORRECTIVE ACTION: Added python3 to satisfy a new LAMMPS build dependency.
# ca-certificates is included for secure network communications.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    gfortran \
    python3 \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    libfftw3-dev \
    libgomp1 \
    ca-certificates && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce image size
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Define a temporary build directory
WORKDIR /build

# Clone the latest development branch of LAMMPS directly into the container
# This is done in a RUN step to comply with the "NO COPY/ADD" instruction.
RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch develop https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git .

# Build LAMMPS from source using CMake
# Enable the required REAXFF package and MPI support.
# Since this is a single-stage build, the build artifacts are created here.
RUN mkdir build-lammps && \
    cd build-lammps && \
    cmake ../cmake \
        -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
        -D BUILD_MPI=on \
        -D PKG_REAXFF=on && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Per instructions, copy the main 'lmp' executable to a system PATH location.
    # This avoids using 'make install' and satisfies the requirement to not symlink.
    cp ./lmp /usr/local/bin/lmp

# Set the final working directory for running the application
WORKDIR /app

# Copy the specified example files from the cloned source into the WORKDIR
# This is also done via a RUN command with 'cp' to meet constraints.
RUN cp /build/examples/reaxff/HNS/* .

# Clean up the build directory to reduce final image size
RUN rm -rf /build

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes
# These settings prevent OpenMPI from trying to use shared memory mechanisms (vader)
# or high-performance interconnects (openib) that are not typically available,
# ensuring it falls back to TCP/IP for communication between pods.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl="^openib"
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml="ob1"

# Provide a default command to allow for interactive use of the container
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: lammps-reaxff-hns
  namespace: default
spec:
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: lmp -v x 8 -v y 8 -v z 8 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax

  logging:

  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: c6i.16xlarge
  size: 1

flux-minicluster-manifest.item:
# This MiniCluster manifest is designed for a single-node LAMMPS experiment
# running on an AWS CPU instance within a Kubernetes cluster.
# It is configured to be deployed by the Flux Operator.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the MiniCluster job.
  name: lammps-reaxff-hns
  # Deployment will occur in the default namespace.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster set. For a single-node run, this is 1.
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI tasks (ranks) for the job.
  tasks: 4

  # Keep pods and services after the job is complete for debugging and inspection.
  cleanup: false

  # Configure logging verbosity for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Ensures that if an unknown setting is found, the MiniCluster will fail to validate.
    strict: true

  # Define the application container to be run within the Flux instance.
  # The Flux Operator will create one container per pod defined by 'size'.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # The command that will be wrapped by 'flux run'.
      # The user does not need to add 'flux run' or 'flux submit'.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite

      # This is the main job container, not a separate pod for launching.
      launcher: false

      # No resource requests or limits are specified.
      # The pod will be in the 'Burstable' QoS class and can use available node resources.

The 64-core ARM instance (28s) performed better than the 48-core AMD instance (33s). This attempt will test a high-performance 32-core Intel instance (c6i.16xlarge) to evaluate the third CPU architecture and determine if it offers a better performance-per-core or overall runtime.

The 64-core ARM Graviton3 instance (hpc7g.16xlarge) delivered the best performance at 28s. Subsequent tests on high-end AMD (33s) and Intel (46s) instances with fewer cores were slower. This indicates that for this specific LAMMPS workload, the combination of high core count and the Graviton3 architecture is optimal among the available choices.
